title: A One-Two Punch: New Drug Overfeeds—Then Starves—Cancer Cells
gist: A short teaser on a Nature Chemical Biology paper from University of Texas biochemists describing a drug that attacks glycolysis — the oxygen-independent shortcut cancer cells prefer even when oxygen is available — using a two-step targeting-plus-payload design modeled on antibody-drug conjugates but intended to avoid their drawbacks.

insights.claim: Cancer cells preferentially run glycolysis, splitting glucose molecules in half, even when oxygen is present, which makes that pathway a selective drug target that spares normal aerobic cells.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Metabolic selectivity is an orthogonal targeting axis to receptor expression — a differentiated angle for oncology pipelines crowded around surface antigens.
insights.quote: cancer cells tend to prefer this shortcut even when oxygen is present, which makes it a tempting target for treatments

insights.claim: University of Texas biochemists have published a drug in Nature Chemical Biology that acts on the glycolysis pathway in cancer cells.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Early-stage academic asset — watch for licensing or spinout activity around UT's metabolic oncology work.
insights.locator: Now a new drug described in a paper

insights.claim: The new drug adapts the two-step antibody-drug-conjugate logic — antibodies that home only to cancer cells before releasing a payload — while the piece explicitly notes ADCs carry drawbacks the new approach is meant to address.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A credible next-generation-of-ADC narrative is a live investment theme; the specific drawback being solved is the thing to verify in the paper.
insights.quote: These compounds act like biological smart bombs, using antibodies to target only cancer cells before delivering their payload of chemotherapy.
insights.locator: The drug, developed through research led by biochemists

insights.claim: The two-step mechanism is presented as generalizable beyond oncology and could be applied to fighting other diseases.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Platform optionality rather than a single-indication asset — the valuation argument for any spinout hinges on this claim holding.
insights.quote: The two-step process could help fight other diseases as well
